content.text:
`timeoutErrorMessage` now works in Node.js. The Node adapter (`lib/adapters/http.js`, the request-timeout handler) always used the hard-coded "timeout of Xms exceeded" text. It now uses `config.timeoutErrorMessage` when one is set, the same way the browser adapter (`lib/adapters/xhr.js`) already does. Without a custom message, the error text is unchanged.

I checked it with a small script against a local server that never responds:
- An instance created with `timeoutErrorMessage: 'Custom'` rejected with `Custom` (code `ECONNABORTED`).
- A request with only `timeout: 200` still rejected with `timeout of 200ms exceeded`.

I started the existing Node adapter test suite (`test/unit/adapters/http.js`), but it ran past the 2-minute limit, went to the background and printed no results. So it's unconfirmed whether those tests pass with the change.

The config-merging code (`lib/core/mergeConfig.js`) lists this option under a misspelled name, `timeoutMessage`. That doesn't affect this bug: string options still pass from `axios.create(...)` to each request, which the test above shows. I left it alone to keep the change minimal.

content.text:
The fix stands; no further code changes were needed. On the full Node adapter test run (`test/unit/adapters/http.js`), 57 tests pass and 2 fail. Neither failure points to a problem with the fix:

- **"should respect the timeoutErrorMessage property" (line 125):** this existing test sets `timeoutErrorMessage: 'oops, timeout'` but asserts the error reads `'timeout of 250ms exceeded'` (line 149). It was written to the old behaviour, so it fails now that the custom message is used. I didn't edit it, since you asked me not to modify existing tests; it needs its expected message changed to `'oops, timeout'`.
- **"should support max content length":** this one fails the same way without my change (the server returns status 400 instead of the expected size error), so it's an existing problem unrelated to this bug.

The earlier background run was stopped because the test runner never exited on its own; adding `--exit` let it finish in about 5 seconds.
